info.description:
Local viewer for log, metric and trace files: NDJSON, EVTX,
XML, and rule-driven text logs, queried through DuckDB.
The OpenAPI spec is the source of truth for the generated
TypeScript client used by the React frontend.
info.title: obs-viewer API

get.description: Lists directory contents (or zip-archive contents when the path points at a .zip file). Browsers cannot access the local filesystem; this endpoint is how the file picker enumerates folders.

parameters.description: absolute path to list; defaults to the user home directory
parameters.name: path

post.description: Reruns the query against DuckDB and writes the result to output_path via COPY ... (FORMAT JSON, ARRAY false).
F13 — drops the running binary into target_dir so a single zip can carry both data and viewer.
post.summary: Copy the binary alongside exported data

get.description: Returns the DISTINCT value set per requested field (default list when `fields` query param is absent). Fields whose distinct count exceeds the cap (30) are returned with an empty array — signal to the caller that the field is too high-cardinality to be useful as a literal value list. Feeds the query builder's value-suggestion datalist.
get.summary: Distinct sample values for low-cardinality fields

parameters.description: comma-separated list of field names; default: service.name,host.name,SeverityText,log.level,event.category,_source_format
parameters.name: fields

get.description: Returns every file the engine currently has loaded plus the auto-detected timestamp column.

post.description: Runs every ingest adapter's detection against the file and reports each one's score and reason, the first non-blank line as the parser sees it, and any encoding trait that commonly breaks matching (BOM, CRLF, NUL bytes, invalid UTF-8). Read-only: nothing is loaded. This is what the UI shows when a load fails, and it is the input to the rule builder.
post.summary: Explain how a file was, or was not, matched

post.description: Loads a single file by absolute path. Supports virtual zip paths in the form `C:\foo.zip|inner.ndjson` — the inner entry is extracted next to the zip and then ingested. Dispatches through the ingest layer so non-NDJSON formats (EVTX, XML, block, line) are handled too.
Bulk load. Each file is ingested through the dispatch layer; unsupported entries land in `errors` rather than aborting the load.
post.summary: Load every supported file in a directory or zip

post.description: Toggles whether a loaded file participates in subsequent queries. Cheaper than unload+load — the table stays in DuckDB, just excluded from UNION ALL.

Same filter set as /api/query, aggregated into time buckets. The bucket width is derived from the span of the filtered data so the bar count stays bounded, and is reported back as interval_seconds. Returns an empty buckets array — never an error — when no timestamp column is detected or nothing matches, so a missing histogram can never be the reason a query fails.
post.summary: Record counts over time for the current filter

parameters.description: same shape as /api/query; offset and limit are ignored
parameters.name: body

get.description: Returns one manifest per enabled module in Add() order. The SPA reads this at boot to decide which tabs to render and to inject the branding stylesheet + favicons.

post.description: Per field: how many rows carry a usable value, an approximate distinct count, and how many of the enabled files declare the field at all. Uses the same filters as /api/query, so the profile describes the rows on screen. One scan covers every field; value distributions are fetched separately per field via /api/profile/values.
post.summary: Profile every field over the current result

parameters.description: same filters as /api/query, plus an optional field subset
parameters.name: body

post.description: A field's top values with counts, over the rows the current filters select. NULL and empty are excluded — the profile already reports the fill rate, and repeating it here would crowd out the values that carry information. Fetched per field, on demand, because each one needs its own GROUP BY.
post.summary: Most common values for one field

parameters.description: same filters as /api/query, plus the field
parameters.name: body

post.description: Runs the assembled filter set (field clauses, time window, optional free-text search) against the UNION ALL of enabled files. Sort, offset, and limit drive paging. Free-text search uses DuckDB ILIKE on a TRY_CAST-VARCHAR'd row.

get.description: Every rule currently loaded from parsers.d, with the file it came from. Used by the rule builder to warn before a name collides with an existing rule.

post.description: Runs a candidate rule over sample text through the real line adapter and returns the rows, the per-line verdict (parsed or folded into the previous record as a continuation), and any timestamp that the layout rejected. Nothing is written.
post.summary: Preview what a rule would produce

post.description: Writes the rule as a YAML file next to the binary and reloads the parser registry, so it applies to files loaded afterwards without a restart. The rule name is normalized into a filename; a rule that fails to compile is not left on disk. Existing files are only replaced when overwrite is set.

Derives a candidate line rule — regex with named captures, plus a Go time layout — from pasted sample lines. Nothing is written; the result is a starting point for the builder, meant to be corrected against the preview.
post.summary: Infer a rule from sample lines

get.description: Persisted to obs_viewer_settings.json next to the binary. Only the fields present in the POST body are updated.

post.description: Persisted to obs_viewer_settings.json next to the binary. Only the fields present in the POST body are updated.

get.description: MIN/MAX of the active timestamp column across the UNION ALL, plus the list of timestamp-like columns the engine detected.
GET returns the column the engine currently sorts by. POST overrides it; the engine silently falls back to the default if the requested field is absent from the loaded files.
get.summary: Get or set the active timestamp column

post.description: GET returns the column the engine currently sorts by. POST overrides it; the engine silently falls back to the default if the requested field is absent from the loaded files.
post.summary: Get or set the active timestamp column

get.description: Reports whether a newer release exists. Read-only — obs-viewer never downloads or installs anything. Returns enabled=false when the check is switched off, which the UI must distinguish from "up to date".
Lightweight liveness endpoint. The frontend uses this to drive an adaptive 30s / 5s healthcheck.

name.description: Name is the adapter name, e.g. "ndjson", "line".

reason.description: Reason is why, in one sentence.
reason.example: none of 5 rule(s) matched any of the first 40 non-blank lines: iso-bracket, dashdate-level

score.description:
Score is what Detect returned: 0 declines, 100 is an exact magic
match. The highest score wins, ties broken by name.

chosen.description:
Chosen is the adapter that would handle the file, empty when
nothing matched.

first_line.description:
FirstLine is the first non-blank line as the parser sees it,
after BOM removal and CRLF folding.

notes.description: Notes are encoding traits that break matching invisibly.

distinct.description:
Distinct is approximate (HyperLogLog). The question it answers is
"identifier or category?", which does not need the last digit.

files.description:
Files and FilesTotal say how many enabled files declare the field
at all — a different fact from its fill rate, and often the more
useful one.

present.description:
Present counts rows with a usable value — not NULL, not empty.
The same rows the `exists` operator selects.

top.description:
Top caps how many values come back. Defaults to, and is capped
at, 50.

total.description:
Total sums the returned values only, not the whole field — it is
the denominator for the shares shown beside them.

start.description: Start is the bucket's first instant, ISO-8601 UTC.

field.description: Field is the timestamp column the buckets were built on.

interval_seconds.description: IntervalSeconds is the bucket width chosen for this span.

min.description:
Min and Max bound the buckets, so a drag-select can map a pixel
back to an instant without re-deriving the range.

total.description:
Total sums the buckets. Lower than the query's total_count by
however many matching records have no usable timestamp.

status.description:
Status is "parsed" when the line opened a record, or
"continuation" when it was appended to the previous record.

ts.description: TS is the raw captured timestamp text, before the layout runs.

ts_error.description: TSError is why that text could not be turned into a timestamp.

error.description:
Error is set when the rule itself is unusable, e.g. the regex
does not compile. Reported in-band because that is an ordinary
state while editing.

fields.description: Fields are the capture names in regex order.

parsed.description: Parsed and Continuation count the sample lines by status.

timestamp_errors.description:
TimestampErrors counts parsed lines whose timestamp the layout
rejected — rows that would load with no time on them.

truncated.description: Truncated reports that the field list hit the cap.

message_field.description:
MessageField names the field non-matching lines are appended to.
Defaults to "message".

parse.description:
Parse must capture the timestamp as (?P<ts>...). Every other
named group becomes a field.

sample.description:
Sample is the text the rule was inferred from; saved into the
rule file as a header comment.

ts_assume_tz.description: TsAssumeTZ names the zone for timestamps that carry none.

ts_layout.description:
TsLayout is a Go time layout — the reference time spelled out,
e.g. 2006-01-02 15:04:05 — not a strftime pattern.

ts_use_mtime_date.description:
TsUseMtimeDate supplies the date from the file's modification
time, for formats carrying only a time of day.

ts_use_mtime_year.description:
TsUseMtimeYear supplies only the year, for formats carrying month
and day but no year.

warnings.description: Warnings are advisory — an ambiguous date order, a missing year.

dir.description: Dir is the parsers.d directory the rules were read from.

overwrite.description: Overwrite replaces an existing rule file of the same name.

rules.description: Rules is how many line rules are loaded after the save.

available.description: Available is true only when latest is confidently newer.

checked.description:
Checked is false until a check completes, so "unknown" is
distinguishable from "up to date".

latest.description: Latest is the newest published release, absent if unknown.

repository.description:
Repository is the project's page. A destination for a person to
click, not something the binary fetches.
